my-0dJK.title: Google car: grey car, long front antenna
my-0dJK.summary: A unique grey car with a long front antenna, in Gunung Mulu National Park in Sarawak.

my-1Mkw.title: Language: Malay in Latin script
my-1Mkw.summary: Malay uses Latin letters and is very close to Indonesian. They are practically indistinguishable unless you speak one.

my-3C19.title: Flags: state flags
my-3C19.summary: State flags show up fairly often, so they are worth learning.

my-4Be2.title: Street: blue cylindrical containers
my-4Be2.summary: Towns on Labuan island are dotted with blue cylindrical containers.

my-4IDp.title: Pole: 2-1 insulators, long diagonal wooden brace
my-4IDp.summary: On Borneo, poles have two insulators on one side and one on the other, plus a long diagonal wooden support. Only in Sarawak. Indonesian poles look similar but are usually not wooden and have small or no diagonal supports.

differs.how: Indonesian poles are usually not wooden, with small or no brace

my-4IWF.title: Street sign: postal code on the sign
my-4IWF.summary: Postal codes appear on most street signs, and they help to place you.

my-5Y5B.title: Road lines: double white centre line
my-5Y5B.summary: Double white centre lines on two-lane roads. The only Southeast Asian country that does this.

my-7iWU.title: Bin: leaf logo
my-7iWU.summary: Bins with a logo like leaves are in Perlis and Kedah, in the northwest of the mainland.

my-AlbW.title: Pole: thin metal with two parallel tops
my-AlbW.summary: Thin metal poles with two parallel pole tops are only in Sabah, on Borneo.

my-DVpF.title: Pole: black sticker saying TEL TNB
my-DVpF.summary: Black stickers with TEL TNB at the bottom are found only in Johor, in the far south of the mainland.

my-Dwit.title: Pole: black or white sticker
my-Dwit.summary: Electricity poles often have black or white stickers, sometimes with red-and-white or red-and-blue stripes below the black one.

my-FTvY.title: Road: thick yellow bars
my-FTvY.summary: Thick yellow bars that are almost exclusive here. Very rarely seen in Hong Kong and the UK.

my-Fn5n.title: Pole: black sticker on the mainland
my-Fn5n.summary: Black pole stickers are most common on the mainland. On Borneo they only exist in Gen 4 coverage.

my-FqOz.title: Pole: white sticker on Borneo
my-FqOz.summary: White pole stickers on electricity poles only occur in Sarawak, on Borneo.

my-GMuK.title: Language: Chinese characters on signs
my-GMuK.summary: Chinese characters are often seen on signs because about a quarter of the population is of Chinese descent. Indonesia has far fewer.

my-GNKN.title: Kerb: black-and-white painted
my-GNKN.summary: Black-and-white painted kerbs are common. Many other Asian countries have them too.

my-H5tX.title: Bollard: black, white, grey and red
my-H5tX.summary: Bollards usually use black, white, grey and red. Several varieties exist but the layout is mostly the same.

my-LlHN.title: Direction sign: yellow hexagon road shield
my-LlHN.summary: A typical direction sign with a yellow hexagonal highway shield. The hexagon shield is unique here.

my-PHYA.title: Lamp post: triangular metal support
my-PHYA.summary: Lamp posts with a triangular metal support are mainly on the mainland.

my-SLFX.title: Bin: sunny landscape logo, Alam Flora
my-SLFX.summary: Bins with a sunny landscape logo and the words Alam Flora are in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo is sometimes missing, leaving just the name.

my-TekU.title: Kilometre marker: white and blue
my-TekU.summary: Kilometre markers are white and blue, and the hexagon shield is often visible. Unique colour scheme.

my-VXzD.title: Lamp post: boomerang-shaped metal support
my-VXzD.summary: A lamp post with a boomerang-shaped metal support is found in Sarawak, more often outside Kuching.

my-VZEz.title: Bin: S-shaped logo
my-VZEz.summary: Bins with an S-like logo are in Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor, in the south of the mainland.

my-X4Fj.title: Direction sign: black-and-white striped post
my-X4Fj.summary: Signposts are almost always painted with black and white stripes. Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India, Nepal and Bangladesh have them too, so check other clues.

my-ZWP5.title: Landscape: very mountainous roads on Borneo
my-ZWP5.summary: If you know you are on Borneo, a very mountainous road points to Sabah. Sarawak has flatter roads, with mountains usually far away.

my-c4nQ.title: Lamp post: two small circles on the support
my-c4nQ.summary: Lamp posts with two small circles on the support are mainly on the mainland.

my-lopw.title: Street sign: yellow arrow with black outline
my-lopw.summary: Yellow arrow-shaped street signs with a black outline are specific to Johor. The arrow shape itself is unique here in any colour. In southern Negeri Sembilan only the tip is black.

my-m7su.title: Street sign: green arrow, yellow JKR hexagon
my-m7su.summary: Green arrow-shaped street signs with a yellow hexagon marked JKR on the left are found in Sabah, on Borneo.

my-r0EY.title: Plate: black with two white sections
my-r0EY.summary: Black plates with two white sections, still visible when blurred. Indonesian plates can be black too but have three white sections.

differs.how: Indonesian black plates have three white sections

my-rEQ4.title: Sign: stop says BERHENTI, yield BERI LALUAN
my-rEQ4.summary: Stop signs say BERHENTI and yield signs say BERI LALUAN. Both are unique here.

my-tGn7.title: Route marker: letter before road number
my-tGn7.summary: Each state, except the three federal territories, has its own road numbering with a unique starting letter. Sabah also has A roads, but only A2 and A7.

my-vYmT.title: Landscape: isolated rock hills in flat land
my-vYmT.summary: Isolated rock formations rising abruptly from flat land, near the Thai border in Perlis.
